notes: Recorded here because refusing an instruction is a decision that spends credibility rather than alpha, and because the alternative would have destroyed 56 percent of the corpus on the strength of a document rather than a measurement. hypothesis: assumedPriorityFeeLamports of 200000 is the priority fee a BUILD_CUSTOM leg actually pays
motivation: the fee was never measured and could not be: priorityFeeLamports() multiplied the routers unit price by a null unit limit and returned zero for every Jupiter route because Jupiter never sends SetComputeUnitLimit
sample_source: live /swap/v2/build responses at four notionals plus a live SVM calibration and three settled mainnet transactions
sample_window: SOL to USDC routes at 0.01 0.02 0.05 and 0.1 SOL built within one minute
metric: charged priority fee in lamports derived from each routes own bytes
result: 3018 to 3564 lamports against an assumed 200000 - a 56x overstatement
action_taken: set assumedPriorityFeeLamports to 8000 as a documented fallback and made the byte-derived value the primary source
notes: The applied compute limit derives to exactly 1006000 on every observed route: 7 instructions of which 2 are builtin at 3000 units and 5 are BPF at 200000. That figure is corroborated three ways - a live SVM charged 6000 for two builtins and 9000 for three and clamped an explicit 2000000 to 1400000 all measured off the payer balance at one lamport per unit; a real Jupiter route logged consumed 183 of 1000499 compute units which is 1006000 less the early instructions; and three settled mainnet transactions reproduce their fees to the lamport. This is an availability correction and not an outcome-driven one: no return series was consulted. It moves costs DOWN which flatters the strategy,  so it is recorded with more care rather than less. 8000 is roughly 2.2x the dearest observed fee and covers a doubling of the routers unit price; it is a fallback only,  because the per-leg fee is computable from the bytes and a constant is still an assumption. Every economic number produced before this change carried a phantom 99 bps per leg and 198 bps per round trip at the 0.02 SOL size.

hypothesis: contextSlot is present on a BUILD_CUSTOM response and can be required before an observation is accepted

metric: fraction of observations where context_slot is populated
result: 0 of 22177 - Jupiter /swap/v2/build does not return it at all
action_taken: removed contextSlot from the hard refusal in missingBuildField and moved it into legIsConfirmatory as a blocker on confirmatory grading only
notes: This was caught by an end-to-end test rather than by the unit tests,  which passed: the unit fixtures supplied a contextSlot because the directive said the field existed. The first live build after the change came back MISSING_CONTEXT_SLOT,  and the corpus then showed the field has never once been populated. As written it would have refused 100 percent of builds and halted all collection while every unit test stayed green. That is the same defect already recorded as MT001 and MT002 and the invariant is explicit: absence of a provider field is a fact about the provider,  not about the token,  and never hard-vetoes. The field remains genuinely load-bearing - an offline replay needs a slot to stand at or lookup tables extended since will not resolve - so its absence blocks the row counting as evidence rather than blocking the row existing. No confirmatory window can open until a slot source is found.

hypothesis: the candidate sampler must spread across pools before deepening on any one
motivation: the first development window opened the SAME three mints on consecutive cycles; the sampler ordered by slot with no reference to what it had already sampled

A hundred paths across three pools is three outcomes with a hundred observations of them, and the 100-path threshold would have been met while supporting no claim about a population. The cap is 3 rather than 1 because the same pool at a different hour is a different market, so a repeat is informative but not independent.

hypothesis: the frozen 0.02 SOL notional is too large relative to the pools the sampler reaches
motivation: the entry impact bound was computed and DISCARDED (`void impact`) with hardcoded zeros written to every trajectory row; wiring it through revealed entries at 70-112% of pool quote reserve
sample_source: development window V1 candidates
metric: entry quote in as a fraction of effective quote reserve
result: 70.5% and 111.7% against a 0.5% small-impact bound; haircuts of 14110 and 22346 bps
action_taken: NONE YET - recorded, and the real bound is now stored per trajectory instead of a hardcoded zero. Neither the notional nor a minimum-depth filter has been changed.
notes: A round trip at 112% of a pool's quote reserve measures our own footprint rather than the venue, and any counterfactual exit built on it is dominated by self-impact. The fix is either a smaller notional or a minimum effective-quote-reserve admission gate, and BOTH are preregistered acts that must be decided before the next window rather than after seeing which produces better numbers. Deliberately left open.

hypothesis: the entry must be small relative to the pool it enters
motivation: the entry impact bound was computed and discarded; wiring it through showed the sampler was selecting drained pools where a 0.02 SOL entry is 6-170% of the quote reserve
sample_source: 29 readable confirmed-migration candidates, depth read live
metric: entry quote in as a fraction of effective quote reserve
result: 19 of 29 pools held 18-57 SOL (entry 0.1%); 10 were drained to 0.01-0.32 SOL (entry 6-170%)
action_taken: admission now refuses when the entry exceeds SMALL_IMPACT_BOUND of the effective quote reserve, and refuses on an unread reserve
notes: NOT a new threshold. SMALL_IMPACT_BOUND (0.5%) was already frozen in this repository for counterfactual validity and was being computed and discarded while the admission gate ignored depth entirely; this makes one threshold consistent with itself. Chosen on POOL DEPTH, before any policy outcome was examined, and it does not starve the study: 19 of 29 candidates qualify. Supersedes the open item MT039, which asked whether the notional was wrong - it is not, the candidate selection was.

hypothesis: the exploration arm must actually run, and its budget must survive a restart
motivation: allocate() existed, was tested, was pure, and no production caller invoked it, so 100% of the budget went to the ranking while pnpm exploration:status - an alias for cohort:status - reported on a different question
sample_source: the exploration entitlement ledger, empty at the time of the change
metric: fraction of opened trajectories drawn by the random arm
result: 0 of 187 - no trajectory had ever carried an arm, because the arm had never been invoked
action_taken: wired allocate() into the collector open path and made the entitlement a database ledger keyed by window and stratum
notes: NOT a threshold change. EXPLORATION_FRACTION stays at the frozen 25%; what changed is that the frozen fraction is now applied instead of being computed by nobody. The ledger is in the database because the collector is a daemon that restarts and an in-memory entitlement makes 25% mean "25% of whatever happened between crashes".

hypothesis: exploration entitlement must be earned by rows that exist, not by rows that were selected
motivation: the first live cycle selected eight candidates, the depth gate refused all eight, and the ledger still recorded granted 3 consumed 0 - so every cycle would add budget for rows that never existed
sample_source: one live collector cycle under the selection-based grant
metric: granted entitlement units versus trajectories opened
result: 6 units granted across two strata against 0 trajectories opened
action_taken: moved the grant after the open loop and keyed it on rows actually opened; deleted the 6 phantom units, none of which had been consumed
notes: Found by RUNNING the thing rather than by reading it. Deleting the phantom grants lost no history because consumed was zero on both rows; had anything been spent the script refuses rather than zeroing. Consequence, stated: the first window is now all exploitation, visibly, because a stratum earns its budget from the cycle before.

hypothesis: a signature listing whose newest slot is below the exit slot indicates an incomplete listing
motivation: the first live full-event-replay run refused a real pool with EVENT_LIST_INCOMPLETE
sample_source: one armed pool, 3Ydh3BiTFP4h, entry slot 439739457
metric: newest listed slot versus exit slot
result: newest listed slot 439484116, exit slot 439740409 - the pool had not traded in 255341 slots
action_taken: removed the forward-bound refusal; only an empty listing is refused now
notes: The hypothesis was WRONG and the run proved it. getSignaturesForAddress is queried newest-first with no cursor, so a newest slot below the exit is the observation that nothing traded, not evidence of a gap. The check was rejecting quiet pools - the one case where the replay is trivially exact. The backward bound (the listing must reach back past the entry) is unchanged and still refuses.

hypothesis: the reject panel must be prospective, so its horizons and metric are fixed before any row is admitted
motivation: reject:panel-v2 aliased trajectory-status.ts, which answers what the OPENED trajectories are doing - the opposite population - and the prospective panel did not exist at all
sample_source: reject_tracking, which records that a token was rejected but not the state it was rejected on
metric: rows carrying the snapshot the rejection was made on
result: 0 of 1191281 - the state was never stored, so every score would be computed against state fetched later
action_taken: added prospective_panels, prospective_samples and prospective_sample_marks; the rule is a literal in source frozen at 2026-08-16T00:00:00Z; admission refuses a row rejected before the rule, and marking refuses an undeclared horizon
notes: The 1191281 existing rows are NOT back-admitted. A panel cannot be made prospective after the fact, and merging them would be exactly the retrospective panel this replaces. Horizons mirror the trajectory mark offsets so both populations are observed on one schedule; the metric is an executable quote rather than a USD price, because 93% of a previous corpus had no route at all.

hypothesis: the mark grid must be able to express the exit-policy comparison it exists to make
motivation: the 8f73cef audit found no constructed path where FLOW_LIQUIDITY_DETERIORATION_V1 exits EARLIER than FIXED_15M_CONTROL at a different mark - and the cause turned out to be the grid, not the policy
sample_source: the mark offsets themselves, before any outcome existed under the current contract
sample_window: no window has opened under contract-d2b2bf4f5f83b0a1
metric: whether a deterioration detected before 15 minutes can be FILLED before 15 minutes
result: impossible on the 1/5/15/30/60 grid: the challenger needs two measured marks to see a drop, so the earliest trigger is 5m, and the first mark after 5m is 15m - the control's own horizon
action_taken: added 3m and 10m horizons, so a drop between 1m and 3m triggers at 3m and fills at 5m
notes: AVAILABILITY-driven, not outcome-driven: no outcome exists under this contract, and the change was forced by P9.2 requiring the challenger to fill at the first LATER valid mark rather than at the one that revealed the deterioration. Pricing it at the trigger books the exit at the one observation the strategy demonstrably could not have traded at. With the old grid the challenger could only ever differ by holding LONGER, and with heavy-tailed returns exiting early is the half of the hypothesis most worth testing. Cost: seven marks per trajectory instead of five.

hypothesis: the candidate queue must be able to reach candidates the gates would admit
motivation: the collector refused EVERY candidate on depth while eleven admissible pools sat untouched under the per-mint cap
sample_source: live effective quote reserves read for all 58 confirmed migrations at 2026-08-17T05:15Z
metric: pools with >= 4 SOL effective quote reserve, which is what a 0.02 SOL entry at the 0.5% bound requires
result: 38 of 58 deep enough; 11 of those still under the cap; deepest 184.7 SOL where the entry is 0.01% of the pool - and the collector refused everything it looked at, at 14.3% to 568.1%
action_taken: candidate ordering sinks a mint whose most recent risk-fact reading refused it for DEPTH; least-sampled-first is preserved within each group
notes: A STARVATION LOOP, not a threshold problem. Least-sampled-first is right, and combined with a gate that PERMANENTLY refuses part of the population it is self-defeating: a drained pool is refused on depth, so it is never sampled, so it stays least-sampled, so it returns to the head of the queue on the very next cycle, forever. The corpus shows both ends at once - one mint at 58 trajectories while eleven admissible pools sat untouched. Sinking rather than excluding, because a pool can recover and a mint that is shallow now is a legitimate candidate later; it just must not block the ones admissible today. NO GATE WAS WIDENED: the 0.5% depth bound, the per-mint cap and the notional are all unchanged.

hypothesis: the entity-adjusted concentration gate must compare a share of SUPPLY, because that is what its limit means
motivation: the first deep pool the repaired window ever saw was refused at 'entity-adjusted share 71.0% vs limit 50.0%' with every other gate passing, and the number was not a share of the token
sample_source: three live mints walked end to end (6zz4T7Vb7Q, 2XVHivUmgW, Eztcckaju2) plus the 11 corpus rows carrying a raw share
sample_window: one instant, before any trajectory opened under contract-cc437a9a9be4ba57
metric: the entity figure expressed as a share of supply, against the raw figure the same gate already accepts
result: the raw share across the corpus runs 11.4% to 47.2% of SUPPLY (mean 30.6%); the entity figure was coming out at 71.0%, 74.9%, 92.5% and 97.3% because concentration() reports over the holders it is handed, not over supply. Rebased: 20.68%, 19.42% and 36.22% of supply
action_taken: measureEntityTier scales the within-holders figure by the examined set's own share of supply, so the number reaching admitCandidate means what the limit means. The limit itself is unchanged at 50%
notes: NOT A WIDENING. concentration() is right to report over the holders it was handed - the number it exists to produce is the GAP between the entity and address readings, and both need one denominator. The defect was handing that figure to a gate whose other input (rawTopHolderShare = held/supply.amount) is a share of supply: two different quantities compared against limits written for one of them. Left uncorrected the entity gate refuses every candidate forever, which is not a strict gate, it is a broken instrument. The GAP survives the rebase and is the point: Eztcckaju2 reads 36.22% entity against 30.91% address, 19 addresses resolving to 16 entities with one funder behind four of them. Program-owned holders stay out of the entity numerator because they belong to no wallet cluster; the RAW tier counts them and both gates run.

hypothesis: the per-mint cap of 3 is enforced over SAMPLES, not over rows that mention a sample
motivation: a fresh window refused RESERVATION_CAP_REACHED on 24 of 25 candidates; the ordinal was reservations + historic trajectories + 1 and an OPENED reservation is already counted as a trajectory
sample_source: trajectory_reservations joined to development_trajectories over confirmed_migrations
metric: mints admissible under a cap of 3
result: 47 admissible before the correction, 124 after; example mint 6zz4T7Vb7Q6M scored ordinal 5 for 2 samples
action_taken: the cap VALUE is unchanged at 3; only the count was corrected so that a sample is counted once (S092)
independent_confirmation: not required - no outcome or return was consulted, and the change was made because candidates were unavailable rather than because results improved
notes: this is a defect repair rather than a threshold move, recorded here because it changes which candidates are admissible and CLAUDE.md requires that to be written down before it lands

hypothesis: MIGRATION_MICROSTRUCTURE_RISK_V1 removes catastrophic launch structures without removing right-tail winners
motivation: every smart-policy input at aaf6d6a was the literal null, so HARD_GATES_RANDOM was the only arm that could enter and the tournament had no economic content
sample_source: no Epitaxy outcome was consulted; the families come from MemeTrans (>40k migrated launches), SolRugDetector and Pump.fun graduation work, and the values come from protocol mechanics
sample_window: no window has opened under this policy
metric: eight decision-bearing conditions, each a catastrophe bound rather than a central tendency
result: creator net selling <= 0 lamports; entity concentration <= 0.60; largest first-buyer entity share <= 0.70; early buyer retention >= 0.20; late sell pressure <= 0.80; migration path entity dominance <= 0.70; mint behaviour safe; mechanics viable
action_taken: registered before the window opens; the policy decides on every trajectory and enters only where all eight hold
notes: REGISTERED BEFORE ANY OUTCOME EXISTS, which is what makes it availability-driven rather than alpha-spending. Every threshold is deliberately EXTREME rather than central - the survivor policy uses 0.35 for entity concentration and this uses 0.60 - because the job is to refuse the launch that is one wallet in a trench coat, not to prefer the tidiest token. Epitaxy's own window C had 2 of 13 paths positive with one ~+14m lamport winner carrying the total, so a filter tuned to raise the win rate would remove the paths that carry the strategy. A test asserts that a volatile-but-sound launch (late sell pressure 0.75, entity concentration 0.55, first-buyer share 0.65) still ENTERS; that assertion fails first if anyone tightens these to improve a summary statistic.

hypothesis: size is chosen from the pool's mechanics rather than fixed at an arbitrary research notional
motivation: the flat 0.02 SOL entry caused depth refusals where the proposed position was an absurd fraction of the pool, removing real market observations for a reason that had nothing to do with the market
sample_source: the size rule is evaluated from one coherent snapshot per candidate; no outcome or return is an input to it
sample_window: no window has opened under the dynamic rule
metric: the largest candidate size satisfying every frozen bound
result: candidate sizes 0.0025 / 0.005 / 0.01 / 0.02 SOL; bounds unchanged at reserve share <= 50 bps, price impact <= 50 bps, bounded-counterfactual impact <= 10 bps, warm round-trip drag <= 400 bps
action_taken: the notional became a rule; every candidate size is evaluated and persisted with the condition that bound it
notes: NO SAFETY BOUND WAS WIDENED. Every limit is the one the fixed notional already had to clear; what changed is that the rule now asks what size fits this pool instead of whether the pool fits one number. 0.02 SOL is retained as the CEILING. An unmeasured bound refuses, so a size whose impact could not be computed is never chosen. chooseSize takes no return, no mark and no future state - the type signature is the guarantee, not the discipline.

hypothesis: two primary entry clocks (T0 and T120) rather than a grid over delays
motivation: the collector's only entry was at the first mechanically valid post-migration state, which buys with no post-migration confirmation at all
sample_source: no outcome was consulted; T120 was chosen from the observation requirement, not from a delay search
sample_window: no window has opened with a delayed arm
metric: paired T0-versus-T120 outcomes within the same mint
result: 120 seconds: long enough to observe post-migration buyer persistence, short relative to the 15-minute primary horizon, and pairable within a mint
action_taken: T0 and T120 are the only primary treatments; 30/60/180/300s are recorded as descriptive snapshots and are NOT entry treatments
notes: A grid over ten delays would spend the multiple-testing budget on a nearly continuous dimension where the winner of a ten-way search at this sample size is noise. Two clocks pair within a mint, which removes the token-selection variance that dominates everything else here. The descriptive offsets are explicitly barred from inference so they cannot become six delays by the back door; a test asserts T0 and T120 cannot share a decision-time snapshot, because reusing one is the obvious optimisation and would silently turn the delayed arm into a relabelling of the immediate one.

hypothesis: the six smart-policy signal inputs are computed from strictly pre-decision data
motivation: independentBuyerPersistence, nonMayhemNetQuoteInflowLamports, effectiveQuoteReserveTrend, executableExitCapacityTrend, continuationSlope and creatorNetSellingLamports were all the literal null at aaf6d6a
sample_source: definitions frozen before any outcome under them exists
sample_window: no window has opened with non-null signals
metric: non-null coverage per field, reported by pnpm policy:coverage
result: persistence window 60s; exit-capacity reference fraction 1.0 of the held position; continuation slope from LOG EXECUTABLE price normalised per second with the pre-existing vertical cap of 5
action_taken: signals are filled from the closed pre-migration curve at T0 and from confirmed post-migration flow at T120, with the SOURCE of every value recorded
notes: The T0/T120 asymmetry is deliberate and is the experiment: at T0 there is by construction no post-migration flow, so filling T0 from later flow would hand it information it could not have had and destroy the comparison. Every null carries a recorded reason, because a null nobody can explain is indistinguishable from a bug and six of them in a row was exactly that. Where Mayhem flow cannot be isolated the answer is null rather than ordinary net flow: an unseparated number answers a question nobody asked.

hypothesis: the per-process RPC bucket no longer needs to pre-divide a budget the shared endpoint budget now divides
motivation: the pre-migration history fetch ran at 3.8 calls/s and one launch with 1,195 pre-migration transactions took about four minutes, so a 100-mint window was not reachable in a day
sample_source: config/source-limits.json own note, plus the measured history-fetch rate on 2026-08-18
sample_window: two mints characterised in the first live cycle
metric: calls per second one process may present to an endpoint
result: solana_rpc was 4/s burst 2, halved explicitly to keep the SUM of two collectors under the documented ~10/s; the note said the real fix was a shared per-endpoint budget and that it was not built
action_taken: raised to 8/s burst 4 now that S079 enforces an endpoint-wide total of 8/s across all processes; the halving had become double counting and capped the system at half the documented limit
independent_confirmation: not required - no outcome or return was consulted; this changes collection speed and cannot change any decision
notes: NO DOCUMENTED LIMIT IS EXCEEDED and no gate moved. Both endpoints document ~10 req/s and the SHARED total stays at 8/s, so the sum across processes is strictly under exactly as before; what changed is that the division is now done once instead of twice. Recorded here rather than treated as a config tweak because it changes how many candidates a window can characterise per day, which changes which candidates are in the corpus.

hypothesis: a truncated signature index must not be reported as a COMPLETE pre-migration history
motivation: the first live window characterised a mint from 296 signatures spanning 25 slots AT its own migration, 197 of the newest 200 failed, and reported COMPLETE with every creation-anchored total written as 0
sample_source: two mints characterised in the first live cycle, then probed directly against the endpoint
metric: whether coverage COMPLETE implies any pre-migration trade was decoded
result: 1 of 2 mints reported COMPLETE over ZERO decoded trades; its bonding curve is closed and the provider index retains only a window around the migration
action_taken: feature version bumped to migration-microstructure-v2: COMPLETE now requires that the oldest signature seen is strictly older than the migration slot AND that at least one trade decoded; a bonding curve cannot be created at or after the slot it migrates in
independent_confirmation: not required - no outcome was consulted; the defect was found by running the collector
notes: This is the exact 'unknown becomes zero' failure the feature layer exists to prevent, and it produced the cleanest-looking launch in the corpus - zero sells, zero creator selling, zero concentration. A short signature page proves only that the INDEX has no more to give, never that the address has no older history. v1 rows are KEPT under their own feature_version as the record of what the defective build believed; nothing was deleted.

hypothesis: mintBehaviourSafe is a mint verdict rather than a null check, so both smart policies can be evaluated at all
motivation: the P2 coverage histogram named mintBehaviourSafe as unknown on 6 of 6 trajectories, which traced to a comparison that can never be true
sample_source: policy_field_coverage over the first profit-discovery window
metric: share of trajectories on which mintBehaviourSafe is known
result: 0 of 6, and 0 of every trajectory this collector has ever opened: the expression was freezeAuthority === null, and FactVerdict is the string union SAFE|HOSTILE|UNKNOWN, so it is always false
action_taken: replaced with the mint's OVERALL verdict: SAFE -> true, HOSTILE -> false, UNKNOWN -> null; extracted to packages/intelligence/src/mintfacts.ts so it is testable without a chain
independent_confirmation: not required - no outcome or return was consulted; the defect was found by a coverage report, not by a result
notes: NOT A THRESHOLD MOVE and not a widening. The field is an input to entry POLICIES, never to admitCandidate, so no safety gate changes: a mint whose overall verdict is HOSTILE now returns false and the policies refuse it on signal, where before they refused it for want of an input. UNKNOWN deliberately stays null rather than collapsing to false - 'we could not read the mint' and 'the mint is hostile' are different facts and only the second is a property of the token. TypeScript permits comparing a string union to null, and the expression lived inside a cycle loop that needs a chain to run, so nothing caught it until coverage was reported per field.

hypothesis: getMultipleAccounts is chunked to the endpoint's MEASURED 5-account bound rather than the spec's 100
motivation: entity-adjusted concentration was unmeasured on 84% of candidates and the refusal read HTTP 429 max usage reached, which was diagnosed as an exhausted account and nearly answered with a subscription purchase
sample_source: direct probe of the configured endpoint, interleaved sizes to rule out an accumulating bucket
metric: share of candidates whose entity tier returns MEASURED with trustworthy=true
result: 0 of 4 before. n=5 OK 28ms, n=20 429, n=5 again OK 27ms, n=6/7/8 all 429, and the same 20 addresses split into 4 batches of 5 resolved 20/20 in 468ms - a sharp per-request cliff between 5 and 6, not a rate effect
action_taken: getMultipleAccountsRaw chunks at 5; after the change the same four mints measured 4/4 with every holder history reaching its earliest signature, entity shares 0.5148 / 0.7260 / 0.0254 / 0.8970
independent_confirmation: not required - no outcome or return was consulted; the defect was found by probing an endpoint, and the fix restores a measurement rather than changing one
notes: NO GATE, THRESHOLD OR MEASUREMENT DEFINITION CHANGED. The concentration limit is still 50% and the entity walk parameters are untouched; the reading simply now happens instead of failing. getTokenAccountOwners passed the top TWENTY holders in one call, so it failed 100% of the time on this endpoint, which made measureEntityTier refuse, which made entityConcentration null, which made BOTH smart entry policies NOT_EVALUABLE. The 429 message says 'max usage reached', which is the wording of an exhausted plan, so this was very nearly answered by buying capacity that would not have helped. Coherence is unaffected: these are independent owner lookups and the coherent path (getMultipleAccountsAtSlot) is untouched - its economic set is four accounts, under the cliff, which is why snapshots never exposed this.

hypothesis: the round-trip cost of a position is a U-shaped function of notional, with a minimum above the 0.02 SOL development size
motivation: the measurement-power directive states that 0.02 SOL sits at the maximum of the cost curve, with ATA rent at 10.2% of notional and priority fees at about 5%
sample_source: 142 stored coherent snapshots (latest per pool) priced offline through the pinned PumpSwap SDK; fixed costs from leg_settlements, simulation_steps, created_accounts and 4,945 stored /swap/v2/build bodies
sample_window: the whole corpus to 2026-08-18; no new collection
metric: total round-trip cost as a percent of notional at 0.02 / 0.05 / 0.10 / 0.20 / 0.35 / 0.50 / 1.00 SOL, plus 0.005 and 0.01 SOL as a below-grid diagnostic
result: MONOTONE INCREASING over the directive grid: 2.69 / 2.88 / 3.26 / 4.02 / 5.14 / 6.23 / 9.61 percent. Below the grid, 2.67 at 0.01 and 2.75 at 0.005, so the true minimum is near 0.01 SOL and 0.02 is 2 bps above it. Neither premise survives: the base ATA closes in the same transaction as the exit swap and the settlements measure 2,063,690 of its 2,067,391 lamports coming back, so rent is locked capital and not a cost; and the router median unit price of 3,810 microlamports per CU against the two-pass frozen limit of 274,782 units is 1,047 lamports a leg, which is 0.01% of a 0.02 SOL notional
action_taken: no threshold changed. The notional stays 0.02 SOL, which is now recorded as the grid minimum rather than as an inherited constant
outcome_data_used: no - no return was consulted; this is the cost side alone
independent_confirmation: the 248 bps fee floor measured here matches the 241.5 bps median AMM drag the P13 true-stateful surface measured through the simulator, on a different instrument and a different sample
notes: EVERY NOTIONAL EXAMINED IS LISTED, including the two below the directive grid, which exist because a monotone grid locates the minimum at or below its smallest point and does not say where. The right arm is impact and it is real: 248 bps of the 269 at 0.02 SOL is the fee tier and 15 bps is impact, rising to 713 bps of impact at 1.00 SOL. Admissibility falls with size under the UNCHANGED frozen bounds - 142 of 142 stored pools can take 0.02 SOL, 118 can take 0.10, 34 can take 0.20, and 2 can take 1.00 - so the large notionals are not merely dear, they are mostly unenterable. The failed-attempt term is reported as UNKNOWN rather than zero because nothing has ever been submitted; at a stressed 20% landed-failure rate it moves the total by 1 bp.

hypothesis: forward returns can be reconstructed from stored snapshots at each cohort horizon well enough to estimate distribution shape
motivation: the confirmatory sample size depends on the coefficient of variation, and the directive supplies an assumed CV of about 15 rather than a measured one
sample_source: decision_snapshots joined to screenings, restricted in SQL to the eight age bands the four cohorts can use
sample_window: the whole corpus to 2026-08-18, 112,584 mints in band
metric: entry and exit selection rules, and the denomination the return is measured in
result: rules frozen BEFORE any statistic was computed: entry is the FIRST snapshot at or after the cohort lower bound within a quarter of the band width; exit is the snapshot NEAREST the upper bound within plus or minus 25% of it; the sampling unit is the mint, one observation per mint per cohort
action_taken: the reconstruction is labelled DEVELOPMENT_RECONSTRUCTED with isEvidence false, and both a USD and a SOL denomination are reported, the SOL series derived from stored buy quotes against the same mint stored USD price within five minutes
outcome_data_used: no - the rules were fixed before any return was computed, and none of them can see a return
independent_confirmation: the derived SOL/USD median of 75.36 over 3,736 quote-snapshot pairs is internally consistent across 115 hourly buckets; it carries the buy leg fee, which cancels in a ratio of two
notes: ENTRY IS FIRST, NEVER BEST, and exit is nearest in TIME, never nearest to a return - the two places where a reconstruction becomes a search. Denomination is not cosmetic: the 5h-24h mean is +0.04% in USD and -1.22% in SOL, and the difference is half the measured cost floor, so a USD-only reading would have compared a USD return against a SOL cost. Censoring is reported rather than avoided: 34.5 / 62.3 / 41.8 / 38.3 percent of mints with an entry have no exit price, and a carry-forward variant prices them at their last observed value. No disappearance is priced as -100%.

hypothesis: the four age cohorts differ enough in dispersion that the choice of cohort changes the sample size a confirmatory window needs
motivation: the directive states that the 2m-60m cohort has the highest CV and is the slowest route to a conclusion, and instructs that the cohort be selected by lowest required n rather than by highest mean
sample_source: the reconstructed distributions from MT058, SOL-denominated, all-screened, observed exits only
metric: required n at 80% power = 7.84 x CV squared, per cohort
result: CV 79.7 / 127.4 / 50.2 / 21.0 for 2m-60m / 1h-5h / 5h-24h / 24h-7d, so required n 49,854 / 127,151 / 19,780 / 3,441. Every cohort is far above the CV of 15 the directive assumed, so the 200-position gate was underpowered by more than the directive itself claimed. The premise that 2m-60m has the highest CV is not confirmed - 1h-5h does - but 2m-60m does have by far the highest DISPERSION, SD 2.43 against 0.09 for 24h-7d
action_taken: 2m-60m is selected as the confirmatory cohort, being the only cohort whose required n is identified (see MT060). The selection is recorded as made on development data and owes an untouched future test per section 16 of 4890af0
outcome_data_used: YES - required n is a function of the observed mean, so this selection is outcome-driven and spends alpha. A hold-out is owed and is recorded as owed
independent_confirmation: not yet - no window has opened under this selection
notes: ALL THREE RULES THAT COULD HAVE SELECTED ARE RECORDED, because only one of them was used. The directive rule restricted to identified estimates selects 2m-60m at 49,854. Dropping the identification restriction selects 5h-24h at 19,780. Sizing against a TARGET edge the size of the measured cost floor instead of the observed mean selects 24h-7d at 89 and 1h-5h at 1,649. They disagree, and which one is right is a question about the confirmatory metric rather than about the market. The tail is the edge, exactly as Correction 2 anticipated: in 2m-60m the top 10 mints of 59,197 carry 83.6% of the summed return and 22.7% of all the gain, the median mint returns -0.22%, and only 32.6% are positive.

hypothesis: a required n computed from a mean whose interval contains zero can be ranked against one computed from a mean whose interval does not
motivation: 7.84 x CV squared divides by the observed mean, and three of the four cohort means have 95% day-clustered intervals containing zero, which puts an infinite CV inside the same interval
sample_source: the same four reconstructed distributions, day-clustered bootstrap at 1,000 resamples
metric: whether the cohort mean 95% interval excludes zero
result: only 2m-60m does, at [+1.72%, +4.78%] over 6 distinct UTC entry days. 1h-5h is [-7.37%, +0.51%] and 5h-24h is [-2.16%, +6.98%]. 24h-7d has no estimable interval at all: its 16,790 mints all enter on ONE UTC day, because a 7-day horizon inside a 10-day corpus can only be satisfied by mints that were already old when collection started, so the day-clustered bootstrap has a single cluster and returns the point estimate as its own interval
action_taken: a cohort whose required n is not identified is marked NOT RANKABLE with the reason stored, and cannot be selected. Two further floors are applied for the same reason: n at least 1,000 and at least 2 distinct UTC entry days
outcome_data_used: no return was consulted to set the rule, but the rule was ADDED AFTER seeing which intervals contain zero, and it does select the cohort with the largest positive mean. That is stated here rather than left to be discovered
independent_confirmation: not required - this restricts what may be ranked and changes no threshold, gate or measurement definition
notes: THIS IS THE FORK IN THIS DIRECTIVE and it is recorded as one. The restriction is defensible on its own terms - an estimate that is not identified cannot be ranked, whichever direction it points - and it is also the single choice that moves the selection from 5h-24h to 2m-60m. The bankroll requirement is not n x notional because positions are not simultaneous: at 79 mints settling per day and a 1-hour hold the concurrent exposure is 4 positions, which is 0.0922 SOL including the 2,067,391 lamports of rent each open position locks and the 3,883,680 lamports of one-time per-wallet accounts

hypothesis: a memecoin strategy can be required to show positive expectancy after removal of its top 1/3/5/10 outcomes and still be the strategy that was measured
motivation: Correction 2 of the directive: section 19 as written requires both positive expected log growth and positive expectancy after the tail is removed, and for a tail-driven asset class those are contradictory
sample_source: the reconstructed 2m-60m distribution, and the three settled windows on record whose signs disagree
metric: which section 19 criteria gate the confirmatory verdict and which are recorded as diagnostics
result: in 2m-60m the top 10 mints of 59,197 carry 83.6% of the summed return and 22.7% of all the gain in the sample. A strategy that survives top-10 removal at n=300 is not this strategy
action_taken: PRIMARY becomes expected log growth per position at frozen fractional sizing with the lower bound of the 95% bootstrap CI above zero. Expectancy after top 1/3/5/10 removal, after the best day removed, after the best five mints removed, and profit factor become RECORDED DIAGNOSTICS that do not fail the gate. Every other section 19 criterion is retained unchanged
outcome_data_used: yes - the tail concentration measured above is the evidence for the change, so this spends alpha and is recorded before any confirmatory window opens
independent_confirmation: not yet - no confirmatory window has opened under the amended gate
notes: THIS IS A WEAKENING OF SECTION 19 AS LITERALLY WRITTEN and it is recorded as one, before collecting, exactly as the directive requires. The justification is the directive own: the edge, if it exists, IS the tail. What is NOT weakened: concentration must be DISCLOSED alongside any positive result, because it determines the drawdown a live operator actually experiences, and a diagnostic that fails is interpreted rather than ignored. No other gate moves - 21 calendar days, multiple market conditions, untouched holdout, drawdown and CVaR, 2x costs, latency and rent stress, zero replay divergence, zero unresolved reconciliation, stable fingerprints, and the full comparison set all stand.

hypothesis: 200 valid completed positions is enough to detect a genuinely profitable strategy at acceptable power
motivation: Correction 1 of the directive computes about 16% power at n=200 for a CV of 15, so the gate as written would reject a working strategy roughly five times out of six
sample_source: the measured per-cohort CVs from MT059
metric: the confirmatory sample size rule
result: the assumed CV of 15 is low for every cohort; the measured values are 21.0 to 127.4, so the implied n is 3,441 to 127,151 rather than 1,670
action_taken: the rule "at least 200 valid completed positions" is replaced by max(300, 7.84 x CV_observed squared), with CV_observed measured on the development window rather than assumed, and the implied n recomputed and reported at the 50 and 100 checkpoints
outcome_data_used: yes - the CV estimates come from reconstructed returns
notes: This RAISES a requirement rather than lowering one, so it spends no alpha in the direction that matters, but it is recorded because it changes what evidence will be considered sufficient. The consequence is the finding in MT064: the sample the corrected rule demands is larger than the calendar can deliver.

hypothesis: a confirmatory window on the selected cohort can be completed inside the 120-day limit section 3.1 imposes
motivation: section 3.1 requires the projection before collecting and forbids beginning a window that cannot finish

result: the bottleneck is eligible signal arrival exactly as the directive predicted and it is not close - 79 distinct mints settle per day at the median, against a simulator that could carry 8,174 and a router budget that could carry 22,511. At required n 49,854 for 2m-60m that is 632 days, or 362 at the best day ever observed. 5h-24h would need 251 days and 1h-5h 1,610

What DOES fit the calendar is sizing the test against a target edge the size of the measured cost floor rather than against whatever this sample mean happened to be - 21 days for 1h-5h, 52 for 5h-24h, 4 for 24h-7d once its corpus spans enough days. That is a change to the confirmatory metric and therefore the operator decision, not this record.

motivation: Phase B premise 1: PumpSwap fees are tiered by SOL market cap from 1.25% down to 0.30%, and the whole 142-pool corpus may sit in the dearest bucket

The 2026-04-28 program upgrade that appended a trailing fee-recipient account is also settled: no stored build predates it (earliest 2026-08-15), and all SIX distinct stored swap shapes - buy 25/26/27, sell 23/24/26 - were rebuilt through the pinned SDK against their own stored snapshots and every one matched its account count, so the verdict is CURRENT_INSTRUCTION_SHAPE rather than STALE. hypothesis: the provider USD market cap can stand in for the program own market cap when assigning a fee tier at 112,584-mint scale
motivation: the tier is selected from effectiveQuoteReserve x baseMintSupply / baseReserve, which needs pool reserves; reserves exist for 413 snapshots and the corpus has 837,876

metric: provider market cap divided by program market cap, and whether the two select the same tier
result: ratio p10 0.961, p50 1.000, p90 1.050; the SAME tier is selected on 98.4% of the 129 pools
action_taken: the tier assignment is made from mcap / derived SOL-USD across 627,876 snapshots and the cross-check is reported first in artifacts/tier-assignment.json
independent_confirmation: the two quantities are computed from entirely different sources - one from a provider feed in USD, one from pool reserves in lamports through the SDK

Of 118,655 mints with a tier inside the 2m-60m window, 4,715 (3.97%) reach tier 1 or better and 2,004 (1.69%) reach tier 2 or better, at medians of 646 and 273 per day. 209,999 snapshots carry no mcap at all and are excluded rather than defaulted. The SOL/USD series is derived from stored buy quotes against the same mint stored USD price and now lives in packages/research/src/sol-usd.ts, so Phase A and Phase B use one derivation instead of two copies.

hypothesis: entering at a better fee tier lowers the round-trip cost floor materially
motivation: Phase B premise 1 puts up to 188 bps of round trip inside the reach of where entries are taken, with no change to screening quality
sample_source: the same 142 stored pools as D70B4A9A 1.1, stratified by the tier selectFeeTier assigns from each pool own market cap, priced offline with exitPricedAgainst unchanged at PRE_BUY_RESERVES
sample_window: the whole corpus to 2026-08-18; no new collection
metric: cost floor per tier across the 0.005-1.00 SOL grid, and admissibility under the unchanged frozen bounds

Depth rises with it: median effective quote reserve 24.3 / 105.1 / 185.1 / 813.4 / 1110.4 SOL, so admissibility at 0.20 SOL goes from 26 of 134 pools at tier 0 to 5 of 5 at tier 1
action_taken: recorded in artifacts/cost-surface-by-tier.json; no bound widened and no threshold moved

hypothesis: an event-triggered entry admits a subpopulation whose conditional mean makes the experiment decidable
motivation: Phase B premise 2: 2m-60m admits about 66% of mints with an entry, so the +3.04% mean is close to the unconditional population mean and measures the absence of a screen rather than the failure of one
sample_source: 555,612 stored snapshots over 120,177 mints; entry at the first snapshot at or after the trigger fires inside [2m, 45m]; exit unchanged at the snapshot nearest 60m of age within +/-25%
sample_window: 2026-08-11 to 2026-08-19, split chronologically: fit 08-11 to 08-14, holdout 08-17 to 08-19
metric: conditional mean net of the tier cost floor, CV_net, required n at 80% power, arrivals per day, and days to required n
result: every cell examined is in docs/PHASE_B_CELL_LEDGER.csv - 630 rows, one per (trigger x population x tier bucket x notional), of which 459 are evaluable. On the population that can actually be entered, ZERO cells pass on a point estimate and ZERO on a holdout lower bound
action_taken: no threshold changed, no window opened, final state NO_DECIDABLE_CELL
outcome_data_used: yes - this is a search over triggers, tiers and notionals and it spends alpha; the frozen thresholds, the chronological split and the expected false-positive count are all recorded here
independent_confirmation: the collector own executable marks corroborate the direction: at the 60-minute offset over 455 admitted trajectories the median mark is -2.7% of notional, which is almost exactly the measured cost floor, and the mean is -17.4% with a p10 of -69.6%
notes: EVERY THRESHOLD IS FROZEN AND LISTED. T1/T2/T3 are the decoded tier thresholds 420 / 1,470 / 2,460 SOL; T4 and T5 add clocks of 600s and 1,800s from first observation; T6 and T7 are momentum controls whose thresholds were set by matching T1 selectivity in the FIT half (18.931 SOL net inflow per 300s and 440 holders per 300s) and were never tuned against a return. T0 is the no-condition baseline and it is not optional: without it a negative conditional mean cannot be told from a population that is negative anyway. The directive printed reference table (8.4 / 13.6 / 20.2 / 11.3 percent) does not reproduce from its own stated formula, which yields 8.6 / 12.8 / 18.0 / 8.9; rows 3 and 4 of the printed table are also mutually inconsistent under any scaling in sigma, so the formula was used and the printed numbers were not.

hypothesis: the conditional means the triggers produce are earned on a population this apparatus can trade
motivation: a fee tier is a property of a PumpSwap pool, and the collector production path is a direct PumpSwap buy against a canonical pool with no bonding-curve builder
sample_source: confirmed_migrations block times against every trigger firing; a mint counts as tradable only when its confirmed migration PRECEDES the entry snapshot
metric: the fraction of firings that were already migrated at entry, and the conditional mean on each population
result: 276 of 158,085 snapshotted mints ever migrated. Of the 4,580 firings of T1, 26 were migrated at entry - 0.57%. The conditional mean flips sign: T1 is +193.2% over all snapshotted mints and -73.2% over the 16 tradable ones; T2 is +324.9% against -28.2%; the T0 baseline is +3.3% against -65.7%. The same flip appears under a fixed one-hour hold instead of the age-based exit, and at every tier: tier 0 -0.03% against -60.15%, tier 1 +79.41% against -94.89%, tier 2 +482.30% against -98.73%
action_taken: the verdict is taken from the tradable population ALONE, and the all-snapshotted figures are reported beside it as the comparison they are
independent_confirmation: the collector own executable marks, on trajectories its risk gates admitted and priced by the pool own arithmetic rather than a mid price, are negative at every offset from 60s to 3,600s
notes: THIS IS THE FINDING, AND IT RETRO-QUALIFIES D70B4A9A. The +3.04% mean of the 2m-60m cohort - the one survivor of that phase four-of-36 cells - is a property of PRE-MIGRATION bonding-curve tokens. 60% of migrations happen inside the 2m-60m token-age window at a median of 6.1 minutes, so the window is right; what is wrong is that 99.8% of the mints in it never migrate at all (276 of 158,085), and a token that spikes to a 420+ SOL market cap in its first 45 minutes and HAS a pool falls back by the 60-minute mark. n is 2 to 16 per tradable cell, which is enough to refuse a cell and not enough to establish a negative edge; what makes the refusal safe is that the sign is unanimous across seven triggers, two exit rules, three tiers and the independent executable marks.

hypothesis: the throughput term, not the conditional mean, is what makes a cell undecidable
motivation: D70B4A9A refused its window at 632 projected days, so the natural expectation was that Phase B would fail the same way
sample_source: per-cell selectivity measured on each population half, against the frozen 79 settled mints per day
metric: days = required_n / (79 x selectivity), with required_n = max(300, 7.84 x CV_net squared)
result: on the TRADABLE population the calendar is not the obstacle - T1 needs 25 days and T2 80 - and the mean is negative, so no cell passes. On the untradable population the calendar IS the obstacle: T1 needs 130 days at the holdout arrival rate and 78 at the fit rate, and that difference is the same corpus measured on two halves of nine days
action_taken: both projections are recorded per cell, and the arrival-rate sensitivity between halves is reported rather than averaged away
outcome_data_used: no - arrival rates consult no return
independent_confirmation: not required; this refuses cells rather than accepting any
notes: A 9-DAY CORPUS DOES NOT PIN AN ARRIVAL RATE. T1 fires on 4.90% of the fit half and 2.94% of the holdout, which is 78 days against 130 - either side of the 120-day limit - so any verdict that turned on throughput alone would be a coin flip with a decimal point. The verdict here does not turn on it, because the tradable mean is negative at every trigger.

hypothesis: a search over 630 cells can be read at face value
motivation: section 4 of the directive requires the expected false-positive count to be stated given the number of cells and the alpha used
sample_source: the cell grid itself
metric: cells x alpha, one-sided on the holdout lower bound
result: 459 evaluable cells at alpha 0.05 gives 23.0 expected false positives across the whole grid and 13.5 across the tradable half. ZERO cells passed, so the search found nothing even before any multiplicity correction was applied

hypothesis: the cost floor computed from stored pool state is the cost a live version would pay
motivation: section 5 of the directive names two costs that cannot be measured from stored data and bite hardest exactly where Phase B is looking
sample_source: none - neither quantity exists in the corpus
metric: quote-to-land slippage, and crowding
result: both UNKNOWN. The surface prices against stored pool state; a real fill lands into a pool that moved, and on a momentum trigger it is moving fast and against you. Stored snapshots cannot see the bots that would have been ahead of you
action_taken: both are recorded as UNKNOWN rather than priced at zero, in every Phase B artifact and in the report, with the statement that every figure in the phase is an UPPER BOUND on what a live version would earn
independent_confirmation: not possible from stored data by construction
notes: Neither is a reason not to have run Phase B, and both are reasons its numbers are ceilings. The adverse selection is specifically that the correlation between the trigger firing and the price having already run is exactly the thing a momentum entry is most exposed to, and momentum entry on Solana memecoins is the most contested strategy on the chain. Recorded here so that a later phase cannot quietly treat the Phase B floor as the live floor.
